explain.say: Your phone, your radio, a hospital X-ray and the sunshine on your face all use the same thing: electromagnetic waves. They are all light, really, just with different wavelengths. Let us zoom from the longest to the shortest.

faq.q: What are radio waves used for?
faq.a: Radio waves carry radio, TV and some communications signals. They have the longest wavelengths in the spectrum.

faq.q: Why can we only see visible light?
faq.a: Our eyes have cells that respond only to wavelengths of about 400 to 700 nanometres, the band we call visible light.
asks: Why can't we see other EM waves?

faq.a: Gamma rays carry a lot of energy. They can knock electrons off atoms, which damages cells and DNA.

faq.q: What is the order of the electromagnetic spectrum?
faq.a: From longest to shortest wavelength: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

faq.q: Do all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed?
faq.a: Yes. In a vacuum they all travel at about 300 000 kilometres per second, the speed of light.

facts: All electromagnetic waves travel at about 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
Visible light spans roughly 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red).
